IA 1/19, CM APPL 2/19 AND IA 3/19 IS SUO MOTO  RECALLED AS PER ORDER DTD 23/01/2020 IN MACA  134/2014  BY ADV SMT.LATHA SUSAN CHERIAN- SC  THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY  HEARD ON 05.02.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE  FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 134 OF 2014 3  2025:KER:12265  JUDGMENT Dated this the 5th day of February, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.721/ 2008 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thodupuzha, is the appellant herein.
(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 30.07.2008.

According to the petitioner, on 30.07.2008 at about 3 p.m., while he was standing by the side of the Kattapana-Thodupuzha road, a car bearing Reg.No. KL 5Q 8613 driven by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit him down.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver, the 2nd respondent is the owner and 3 respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.5,00,000/-.

2
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the documentary evidence, Exts.A1 to A17 were marked.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,33,010/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

9. Heard Sri.Elson Simon, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Smt.
Latha Susan Cherian, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was 2025:KER:12265 working as Agriculturist , earning Rs. 8000/-per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.4000/-.

11. Since he could not prove his job or income as claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.6500/-.
12.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the accident the petitioner sustained compound fracture tibia, closed reduction, head injury,
scalp wound, fracture fibula right bennets, fracture right hand and fracture rib with haemopneumothorax.
He was treated as inpatient for 17 days.
13. As per Ext. A15 disability certificate, the petitioner suffered 20% permanent physical disability.
In Ext. A15 certificate, it is mentioned that the petitioner is having restricted movement in knee joints and mild shortening of left leg.
The Tribunal, however, scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 14%, without assigning valid and cogent reasons.
The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.(See
Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan 2025:KER:12265 Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305)

I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent physical disability Joseph Augusty vs Vijayan K.K on 5 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125583587/
3 of the petitioner is fixed as 20%.
14.
On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 40 years.

Therefore, 25% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 15, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.2,92,500/-.
15. Towards loss of income, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.18000/-, being the income for 4 months @ Rs.4500/-.
Considering the nature of the injuries sustained and the percentage of disability suffered by by the petitioner, the petitioner might have lost income at least for a period of 6 months.
Therefore, towards loss of income the petitioner is entitled to get a sum of Rs.39,000/-(6500x 6 months).
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000./-.
Towards loss of amenities Rs. 20,000/- was awarded 2025:KER:12265 and towards extra nourishment Rs.2,000 was awarded.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 17 days.

Because of the injuries sustained by the petitioner including 4 fractures, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', loss of amenities and extra nourishment and transportation are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.40,000, 25000, 4000 and 8000/- respectively.
18.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

19. Therefore, the petitioners/ appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.4,78,430/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No. 3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs. 4,78,430/- (Rupees Four lakhs seventy eight thousand four hundred thirty Only), along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, less the amount already deposited if any, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.(interest for the enhanced compensation is limited to 8% )
21.
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse 2025:KER:12265 the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
